# download_youtube_videos

[← Command index](README.md)

Download a video, playlist or channel with yt-dlp as MP4 or MP3.

## Synopsis

```
download_youtube_videos <youtube_url> [options]
```

## Description

Hands the URL to yt-dlp. Videos are converted to MP4; with `-a` the audio is extracted
to MP3 instead, with the thumbnail and metadata embedded. Files are written to `-d`,
named `<upload date> - <title>.<ext>` unless `-o` gives a yt-dlp output template.

yt-dlp resumes partly downloaded files, pauses 3-5 seconds between videos, and uses
Deno (from `~/.deno/bin/deno` or `PATH`) for YouTube's download challenge when it is
installed. Any site yt-dlp supports works, not only YouTube.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `<youtube_url>` | URL of the video, playlist or channel to download. |

### Download

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-a, --audio_only` | Extract the audio as MP3 instead of downloading an MP4 video. |

### Output

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-o, --output_file <output_file>` | yt-dlp output template or file name, relative to `-d`; `<upload date> - <title>.<ext>` when omitted. |
| `-d, --output_dir <output_dir>` | Directory to download into; the current directory when omitted. Default: `~`. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-r, --download_archive <download_archive>` | yt-dlp download archive file; videos listed in it are skipped and new downloads are added to it. |
| `-c, --cookie_source <cookie_source>` | Browser to read cookies from (passed to yt-dlp as `--cookies-from-browser`), or the path of a cookies file (passed as `--cookies`). Default: `firefox`. |
| `-s, --sanitize_filenames` | After downloading, rename files in the output directory to remove characters that are invalid in paths. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Download a video into the current directory

```bash
download_youtube_videos "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID"
```

### Download a playlist's audio as MP3 into a folder

```bash
download_youtube_videos "https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAYLIST_ID" -a -d /path/to/music
```

### Download only videos not fetched before, recording them in an archive

```bash
download_youtube_videos "https://www.youtube.com/@channel" -d /path/to/videos -r /path/to/archive.txt
```

### Download with a chosen file name

```bash
download_youtube_videos "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID" -o "My Video.%(ext)s"
```

### Use a cookies file and clean up the file names afterwards

```bash
download_youtube_videos "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID" -c /path/to/cookies.txt -s
```

### Pretend run, without downloading anything

```bash
download_youtube_videos "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIDEO_ID" -p -v
```

## Notes

- `-s` renames every `.mp4` (or `.mp3` with `-a`) file in the output directory, not only the ones just downloaded.
- Under `-p` yt-dlp is not run at all.
